Its money stays inside the month's totals, declared as a count and one combined figure, so the figures still add up.

reference.hint: What the average household spends a month, and how big that household is on the scale above. Balancr divides the first by the second and scales the result to your household, so both have to come from the same edition of the survey. Balancr cannot fetch them: the survey has no interface for it, and the size is a ratio of two columns rather than a published figure.
reference.meanHint: Total consumption spending of the average household, per month. The survey publishes a year, so divide it by twelve.
reference.overridden: Your own figure applies instead of the file's, typed on {{savedOn}}.
reference.size: Average household size on the scale
reference.sizeHint: In basis points: 15066 is 1,5066 equivalent adults. The survey's total spending per household divided by its total spending per consumption unit, which is the same scale as the weights above.
reference.sizeNotANumber: A whole number of basis points between 10000 and 200000.

dayCurve.minMonths: Fewest months with any spend required before a day-of-month shape is trusted.
dayCurve.windowMonths: How many months of history feed the day-of-month spending shape.

drift.persistentMonths: How many consecutive month-ends a portfolio class must sit outside its target band before it's flagged.

household.emergencyFundTargetMonths: How many months of spending the emergency fund is aiming to cover.
household.savingsRateTargetBp: The savings rate the household is aiming for.

hygiene.priceStaleDays: A portfolio price older than this many days is no longer treated as current.
hygiene.recomputationToleranceCents: How far Actual's own total may differ from the recomputed one before it's flagged.
hygiene.reconcileStaleDays: An account not reconciled in this many days has its balance treated as a guess.
hygiene.uncategorisedWarnCount: How many uncategorised transactions are tolerated before it's flagged.

overspend.baselineAlertBp: How far above the norm a category has to run before it's flagged as an alert.
overspend.baselineWarnBp: How far above the norm a category has to run before it's flagged as a warning.
overspend.materialityFloorCents: Amounts under this are ignored, so a tiny envelope running slightly over isn't flagged.
